nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-02.title: Eliminate one variable
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-02.body:
Let $x,y,z$ be the numbers of sophomores, juniors, seniors. In cents, $50x+90y+125z=2500$, i.e. $10x+18y+25z=500$, and $x+y+z=26$ gives $10x+10y+10z=260$. Subtracting: $8y+15z=240$. Since $8$ divides $8y$ and $240$, it divides $15z$, so $8\mid z$. $z=8$ gives $y=15$, $x=3$; $z=16$ gives $y=0$, not allowed. So there are $8$ seniors.

**Answer: 8**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-03.title: Face centers
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-03.body:
A cube with exactly one red face lies on one face but not on an edge of the large cube. On each face these form a $5\times5$ square, so there are $6\cdot25=150$.

**Answer: 150**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-04.title: Cube the sum
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-04.body:
Let $a=\sqrt[3]{9+x}$, $b=\sqrt[3]{9-x}$. Then $a+b=3$ and $a^3+b^3=18$. Since $(a+b)^3=a^3+b^3+3ab(a+b)$, $27=18+9ab$, so $ab=1$: $\sqrt[3]{81-x^2}=1$, $x^2=80$, $x=\pm4\sqrt5$. Conversely, for these $x$, $a+b=t$ satisfies $t^3=18+3t$, whose only real root is $t=3$ (since $t^3-3t-18=(t-3)(t^2+3t+6)$), so both values work.

**Answer: $x=\pm4\sqrt5$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-05.title: Substitute
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-05.body:
Let $y=\sqrt{\frac{x}{1-x}}>0$. Then $y+\frac1y=\frac{13}{6}$, so $6y^2-13y+6=0$ and $y=\frac23$ or $\frac32$. Then $\frac{x}{1-x}=\frac49$ gives $x=\frac4{13}$, and $\frac{x}{1-x}=\frac94$ gives $x=\frac9{13}$. Both lie in $(0,1)$ and satisfy the equation.

**Answer: $x=\frac4{13}$ or $\frac9{13}$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-06.title: Coordinates
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-06.body:
Put $B=(0,0)$, $A=(0,6)$, $C=(7,0)$. The side $CD$ makes a $120^\circ$ angle with $CB$ (which points in the $-x$ direction), so it points at $60^\circ$ above the $+x$ axis: $D=C+8\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)=(11,4\sqrt3)$. Then $AD^2=11^2+(4\sqrt3-6)^2=121+48-48\sqrt3+36=205-48\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $205-48\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-06.title: Law of Cosines via the diagonal
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-06.body:
$AC^2=6^2+7^2=85$, and $\angle ACB$ has $\cos=\frac{7}{\sqrt{85}}$, $\sin=\frac{6}{\sqrt{85}}$. Then $\angle ACD=120^\circ-\angle ACB$, with $\cos\angle ACD=\cos120^\circ\cdot\frac{7}{\sqrt{85}}+\sin120^\circ\cdot\frac{6}{\sqrt{85}}=\frac{-7+6\sqrt3}{2\sqrt{85}}$. By the Law of Cosines in $ACD$: $AD^2=85+64-2\cdot\sqrt{85}\cdot8\cdot\frac{-7+6\sqrt3}{2\sqrt{85}}=149+56-48\sqrt3=205-48\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $205-48\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-09.title: Pair complementary angles
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-09.body:
$\cot(90^\circ-\theta)=\tan\theta$, so $\cot k^\circ\cot(90-k)^\circ=\cot k^\circ\tan k^\circ=1$ for $k=1,\dots,44$. The remaining factor is $\cot45^\circ=1$. The product is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-11.title: Factor the square minus one
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-11.body:
If $17p+1=n^2$ with $n>0$, then $17p=(n-1)(n+1)$, two positive factors differing by $2$. The factorizations of $17p$ into two positive factors are $1\cdot17p$ and $17\cdot p$. The first would need $17p=3$, impossible. So $\{17,p\}$ differ by $2$: $p=15$ (not prime) or $p=19$. Check: $17\cdot19+1=324=18^2$.

**Answer: 19**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-12.title: Vieta's formulas
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-12.body:
Let the roots be $a$, $ar$, $ar^2$. Then $a(1+r+r^2)=8$ and $a^2r(1+r+r^2)=-60$. Dividing, $ar=-\frac{15}{2}$. The product of the roots is $a^3r^3=(ar)^3=-d$, so $d=\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^3=\frac{3375}{8}$. (Such roots exist: $ar=-\frac{15}2$ and the sum condition give $15r^2+31r+15=0$, which has real solutions.)

**Answer: $\frac{3375}{8}$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-12.title: The middle root is a root
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-12.body:
The middle term $m=ar$ satisfies $m^3=$ product of roots $=-d$ and is itself a root. From $\frac{\text{(sum of pairwise products)}}{\text{(sum)}}=m$ we get $m=\frac{-60}{8}=-\frac{15}{2}$. Substituting into the cubic: $-\frac{3375}{8}-8\cdot\frac{225}{4}+60\cdot\frac{15}{2}+d=0$, i.e. $-\frac{3375}{8}-450+450+d=0$, so $d=\frac{3375}{8}$.

**Answer: $\frac{3375}{8}$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-13.title: Middle dimension
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-13.body:
Let the dimensions be $x-1$, $x$, $x+1$. The surface area is $2\big[(x-1)x+x(x+1)+(x-1)(x+1)\big]=2(3x^2-1)=2644$, so $3x^2=1323$, $x^2=441$, $x=21$. The volume is $20\cdot21\cdot22=9240$.

**Answer: 9240**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-14.title: Sophie Germain–style factoring
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-14.body:
$160401=20^4+20^2+1=(20^2+1)^2-20^2=(401+20)(401-20)=421\cdot381=421\cdot3\cdot127$. Since $421$ has no prime factor up to $\sqrt{421}<21$, it is prime and is the largest of the three.

**Answer: 421**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-15.title: Round exponents up to multiples of 3
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-15.body:
$10!=2^8\cdot3^4\cdot5^2\cdot7$. If $n^3$ is a multiple, then $n$ must contain $2^3$ (as $3\cdot3\ge8$), $3^2$, $5$ and $7$. The smallest is $n=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7=2520$, whose cube $2^9\cdot3^6\cdot5^3\cdot7^3$ is indeed a multiple of $10!$.

**Answer: 2520**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-16.title: Equal tangent lengths
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-16.body:
$AB=13$. Let the circle have center $K$, radius $r$, and touch rays $CA$, $CB$ and segment $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$. Since $KD\perp CA$, $KE\perp CB$ and $\angle C=90^\circ$, $CDKE$ is a square, so $CD=CE=r$. Tangent lengths give $AD=AF$ and $BE=BF$, so $2r=CD+CE=(CA+AF)+(CB+BF)=5+12+13=30$, and $r=15$.

**Answer: 15**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-16.title: Exradius formula
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-16.body:
This is the excircle opposite $C$. Its radius is $\frac{\text{Area}}{s-c}$ with $s=15$, $c=13$ and area $30$: $\frac{30}{2}=15$.

**Answer: 15**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-18.title: Pitot and the Law of Cosines
nyciml-2015-16-spring-junior-18.body:
Let $AD=x$, $CD=y$. A quadrilateral with an incircle has equal sums of opposite sides: $5+y=7+x$, so $y=x+2$. In triangle $ABC$, $\cos B=\frac{25+49-64}{70}=\frac17$. $ABCD$ is cyclic, so $\cos D=-\frac17$. The Law of Cosines in $ACD$:
$$64=x^2+(x+2)^2+\tfrac27x(x+2).$$
Multiplying by $7$ and simplifying: $16x^2+32x-420=0$, i.e. $4x^2+8x-105=0$, whose positive root is $x=\frac{-8+\sqrt{64+1680}}{8}=\frac{-2+\sqrt{109}}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt{109}-2}{2}$**
